newsitem.title: USA: North Carolina sues Norfolk Southern.
newsitem.headline: North Carolina sues Norfolk Southern.

text.p: North Carolina Railroad Co said Thursday it has initiated litigation accusing Norfolk Southern Corp of stopping its rental payments when its lease expired.
North Carolina Railroad said the litigation is expected to be expensive and could take years to resolve.
But North Carolina Railroad Secretary and Director maintained the litigation was necessary "if we do not want Norfolk Southern to operate over our line without making payments."
Robert Fort, a spokesman for Norfolk Southern, said the company was reviewing the lawsuit and would not comment except to say it was "surprised" it had been filed.
"We were surprised because we thought discussions were continuing" on a lease extension, Fort said.
North Carolina Railroad said it was asserting rental property ownership, environmental and other claims arising out of the expired lease with Norfolk Southern.

In July, the U.S. District court for the Eastern District of North Carolina invalidated a shareholder-approved lease extension with Norfolk Southern in litigation brought by a North Carolina shareholder.
The agreement called for an $8 million annual rental retroactive to January 1, 1995, with adjustments for inflation thereafter.
North Carolina Railroad did not immediately return a telephone call seeking further comment.
